note: WRITTEN, 217 rows (31 items x resp 1-7), clean gate with one instrument caveat. WORDS and MAPPING: the study's own SPSS file 'AEQ_Study 3.sav' (OSF fuz6h, Data + Syntax/Study 3 Data + Syntax, https://osf.io/download/9sm3b/, sha256 9c2d66b0c6ced8b2a103ce247c942501148a5ca52ccd2cf7e9045aa1a176eb02); variable labels of DAQ1..DAQ31, 31/31 labelled, shipped verbatim except that embedded line breaks in 6 labels (DAQ2, DAQ3, DAQ7, DAQ10, DAQ17, DAQ18) were replaced by a single space; mixed straight/curly apostrophes and the curly quotes around 'worked up' kept as in the file. Code derivation: data/hyatt_2023_aggression.py selects ^DAQ\d+$ from the Study 3 file and lowercases (_norm_item), so item IS the source column name (DAQ5 -> daq5); exempt pattern, mapping_basis=data_labels. Live table equals the .sav cell for cell: 31 items x 7 levels = 217 per-level counts, 0 mismatches (live 11,026 rows; wave 1/2 = the .sav's Study variable). option_text from the value labels (identical on all 31 items): '1 = Extremely uncharacteristic of me' / '7 = Extremely characteristic of me' with the leading 'N = ' stripped; points 2-6 are labelled only by their own number and are left blank. No reverse-keyed items: the .sav's own composites equal the plain mean of the stored items (DAQ_AngryRumination = mean DAQ1-10, 354/354 rows; DAQ_DisplacedAgg = mean DAQ11-20, 355/355; DAQ_RevengePlan = mean DAQ21-31, 349/349), and every item correlates positively with its composite (.24-.86), so anchors ship in the file's direction. STEP 3b INSTRUMENT CAVEAT: 29 of 31 labels are the Denson, Pedersen & Miller (2006) DAQ items (Table 2 of doi 10.1037/0022-3514.90.6.1032, minor wording variants kept as in the .sav, e.g. DAQ16 'take my frustration out at' vs published 'take out my frustration on'). But DAQ5 is labelled 'If I have to resort to violence to protect my rights, I will.' and DAQ11 'I often find myself disagreeing with people.' - both Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire items, in place of the published DAQ's 'Whenever I experience anger, I keep thinking about it for a while.' (Angry Rumination) and 'When someone or something makes me angry I am likely to take it out on another person.' (Displaced Aggression). The data say the labels are what respondents answered, not a labelling slip: DAQ5 correlates .79 with the same file's BAPQ5p (same BPAQ wording, same 1-7 scale) and .50 with BPAQ3p 'If somebody hits me, I hit back', but only .25 on average with the other nine Angry Rumination items (which average .60 among themselves); DAQ11 correlates .61 with BPAQ11v (same wording), its highest correlation with any variable, and .34 with the other nine Displaced Aggression items (.47 among themselves). Shipped as labelled; instrument named DAQ because the study's block and its composites (and the paper's alphas) treat all 31 as DAQ. instructions blank: the deposit's .sav/.sps and the pre-copyedit manuscript (OSF h4qxe, which describes the DAQ in one sentence) carry no DAQ instructions. Single section_id. Administered in English, no language/_translated columns. Rights: originator Denson, Pedersen & Miller (2006), JPSP 90:1032-1051. The copy hosted by the originators' lab (https://www.aggression-irlab.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/DisplacedAggressionQuestionnaireDAQ2006.pdf, sha256 854f355a8fa7e3a22484fb423176057c5cd9687739c220c29e1ac25fa865f3c2) carries only 'Copyright 2006 by the American Psychological Association', a notice about the article, not a term on the instrument (PANAS precedent); no fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution clause located. The two BPAQ items: no restriction located either. Silence = permission; register has no DAQ/BPAQ row and none written. irw-validate --profile upload: ok.
public_note: Items daq5 ('If I have to resort to violence to protect my rights, I will.') and daq11 ('I often find myself disagreeing with people.') are Buss-Perry Aggression Questionnaire items, not the published DAQ's fifth and eleventh items; the study administered them in its DAQ block, the data behave like them (r = .79 and .61 with the same statements in the study's Buss-Perry block), and the study's Angry Rumination and Displaced Aggression composites include them

source_ref: OSF fuz6h (Hyatt et al. 2023, doi 10.1002/ab.22088), Data + Syntax/Study 3 Data + Syntax/AEQ_Study 3.sav (https://osf.io/download/9sm3b/), SPSS variable + value labels of SSIS1..SSIS10 (SSIS8r); instrument O'Meara, Davies & Hammond (2011) doi 10.1037/a0022400
note: Written, 50 rows (10 items x resp 1-5), one disclosed anchor override. WORDS and MAPPING: the study's own SPSS file 'AEQ_Study 3.sav' (OSF fuz6h, Data + Syntax/Study 3 Data + Syntax, https://osf.io/download/9sm3b/, sha256 9c2d66b0c6ced8b2a103ce247c942501148a5ca52ccd2cf7e9045aa1a176eb02, same file as batch_311 siblings). Variable labels of SSIS1..SSIS7, SSIS8r, SSIS9, SSIS10 carry all 10 item wordings (10/10, none truncated); shipped verbatim except SSIS2's label, which carries an embedded line break ('...sexually, or' / 'emotionally.') replaced by a single space. Code derivation: data/hyatt_2023_aggression.py selects ^SSIS\d+r?$ from the Study 3 file and lowercases (_norm_item), so item IS the source column name (SSIS8r -> ssis8r); exempt pattern, mapping_basis=data_labels. All 10 items x 5 levels = 50 per-level counts in the .sav equal the live table exactly (live 3,858 rows, 229 ids, waves 1/2 = 1869/1989). OPTIONS: value labels 1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Neither agree nor disagree, 4=Somewhat agree, 5=Strongly agree, identical on every item except SSIS7's label 2 which the file spells 'Somewhat disgaree' - obvious typo, shipped corrected as 'Somewhat disagree'. Note this 5-point agreement format is the study's own; O'Meara et al. (2011) describe a 4-point scale - shipped what this study administered per its file. ANCHOR OVERRIDE on ssis8r ('I wouldn't intentionally hurt anyone.'): stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED, so option_text is reversed (resp 1 = Strongly agree .. 5 = Strongly disagree). Evidence: the .sav's own composite 'SSIS' (label 'Trait Sadism (SSIS)') equals the mean of the ten stored items for 384/384 complete rows vs 25/384 with ssis8r flipped back; Cronbach alpha of stored items = .78, exactly the paper's reported alpha (.78), vs .70 with ssis8r flipped; ssis8r correlates positively (+.09 to +.23) with all nine sadism items, item-rest r=+.22; and raw reading would put 219/385 respondents at 'Strongly disagree' with not intentionally hurting anyone. The other nine items keep the file's labels. Items ssis3 and ssis7 have no resp=5 in the data (0 responses); option rows for all 5 points shipped since the scale offered them. instructions blank: the OSF deposit (.sav, AEQ_study3_syntax.sps, pre-copyedit manuscript h4qxe, AEQ instrument docs) carries no SSIS instructions; the manuscript says only 'a 10-item self-report measure of various forms of sadism (O'Meara et al., 2011) ... alpha = .78'. Single section_id. English administration, no language/_translated columns. Step 3b: this is the Short Sadistic Impulse Scale (O'Meara, Davies & Hammond 2011, Psychological Assessment 23(2), doi 10.1037/a0022400), NOT Pearson's Social Skills Improvement System; 10 items, unidimensional sadism content, matching the dictionary description. Rights: originator is O'Meara et al. (2011), an APA journal article. No clause reserving a right (fee, permission, NC, ND, no-redistribution) was locatable (web search of the scale name + permission/copyright returned only the article record, ResearchGate/academia copies, ERIC and Swansea cronfa entries, none with terms); a journal copyright notice governs the article, not the instrument (PANAS precedent). Silence = permission; wording taken from the study's own public OSF deposit; no register row written. irw-validate --profile upload: ok.
public_note: Item ssis8r ('I wouldn't intentionally hurt anyone') is stored already reverse-scored, so for it resp 1 means the respondent strongly agreed with the printed statement and 5 strongly disagreed, the opposite of the source file's value labels; higher resp means more sadism on every item
